channel.title: Daybrief
channel.description: AI first. Everything else that matters, twice a day.

item.title: davemessew/AgentFlux: Agentic AI platform for visual workflows and autonomous agents. Run it with Docker on your own computer or…
item.description: AgentFlux is an agentic AI platform for visual workflows and autonomous agents, run on your own computer or server with Docker. Notably, it builds workflows from videos by sending up to 24 frames to a chosen vision model. Why it matters: Lets people keep files and results local while choosing their own language models.

sanjayadanushka712/Ghost-Night: Local-only browser fingerprint & identity rotation toolkit for authorized security testing. Tor/obfs4…
item.description: Ghost Night is a Python toolkit for authorized security testing that rotates browser fingerprints and IPs via Tor or obfs4, with 81 GitHub stars.

item.title: Avail launches ShieldTX privacy tool targeting copy-trading bots on Hyperliquid
item.description: Avail launched ShieldTX, a Hyperliquid privacy tool that creates a separate wallet for each perpetual futures position.

item.title: Voice AI in vogue: Nvidia releases new open transcription model
item.description: Nvidia released Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe, a free open-weight model for up to 40 languages, and Granary v2, an open speech dataset. It handles recordings up to an hour, not live audio, and can tell up to eight speakers apart. Why it matters: Gives developers a free open option for meeting and medical transcription apps, though it lacks live audio.

item.title: XGIMI Jide AI Memory Glasses G1 / Bracelet L1 Go on Sale, Launch Prices Starting at 1,299 / 599 Yuan
item.description: XGIMI's Jide AI Memory Glasses G1 and AI Memory Bracelet L1 went on sale, with launch prices starting at 1,299 and 599 yuan.

item.title: Interested parties, countries can come together to launch AI incident reporting pilot: PM Wong
item.description: PM Lawrence Wong suggested starting AI incident reporting with common incident categories and secure information sharing, learning from aviation.

item.title: xAI is buying out homeowners who promise not to sue over data center noise
item.description: An xAI subsidiary is reportedly offering to buy Mississippi homes if residents don't join a lawsuit over a nearby data center and power plant.

item.title: Objection, your honor
item.description: Meta's updated business terms let it use content from linked websites to train AI; users in the UK and EU may be able to object.

item.title: Attacker Relentlessly Scans for Credentials by Impersonating AI Bots
item.description: A scanner impersonating 32 AI bots, including ones posing as OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta agents, has hunted for exposed credentials since late September. On one day this month, 48% of Cequence-protected organizations received the traffic, per CQ Prime Research. Why it matters: Shows how hard it is for organizations to tell legitimate AI agents on their networks from malicious ones.

item.title: Bank of Canada raises rates to 2.5%, says more could be needed
item.description: The Bank of Canada raised its benchmark rate to 2.5%, its first hike in over three years, and said more increases could be needed.

item.title: Apple Raises MacBook Neo's Starting Price to $649 on Education Store
item.description: Apple has raised the MacBook Neo's starting price on its US online education store from $599 to $649, cutting the education discount to $50.

item.title: Foundry Raises $100 Million for Autonomous Factories
item.description: Foundry, a manufacturing-as-a-service startup founded less than a year ago, raised a $100M Series A led by Marlinspike Partners. It builds automated factories with AI-powered robots organized into work cells for tasks like cabling, fastening and precise placement. Why it matters: Shows companies rebuilding factories around AI robots rather than adding them to existing production lines.

item.title: Anthropic IPO filing warns some risks may be uninsurable. AI coverage will be issue for every company
item.description: Anthropic's IPO filing warns that some AI risks may be uninsurable, and its policies may not provide sufficient coverage for liabilities from model behavior.

item.title: If You're In the UK or EU, Here's How to Object to Meta's AI Training
item.description: Meta's updated business terms allow it to use content from websites linked to accounts for AI training, and UK and EU users can currently object.

item.title: AI giants' funding ambitions test Wall Street's appetite for risk
item.description: Oct 28 : The heavyweights of the AI industry are facing a reckoning on Wall Street, reflecting concerns over who will bear the cost of the artificial intelligence buildout that…

item.title: Singapore proposes AI incident reporting pilot to boost AI safety
item.description: Singapore PM Lawrence Wong proposed a small pilot for reporting AI incidents, starting with a flexible approach rather than a new international framework.

item.title: SAP swaps costly AI models for cheaper alternatives, targets over €2 billion in gains
item.description: SAP is swapping some costly AI models for cheaper ones where performance stays strong, expecting over €2 billion in efficiency gains over two years.

item.title: The Agent SDK
item.description: Cursor has released the Agent SDK, which lets teams define agents in code and deploy them to Cursor infrastructure with one command.

item.title: 10 Months Into AI for GTM That Actually Works: The CRO Matters More Than Ever. Every Other GTM Role Is in Flux.
item.description: About ten months into AI for go-to-market, agents have absorbed much of SDR and first-line support work, while the CRO role remains critical.

item.title: The October inflection point for vibe game development
item.description: The author argues October 2026 marks a turning point for vibe-coding games, citing Claude Opus 5.5's gains in 3D modeling, music and game design.

item.title: Even after PHP2Shell, blast radius matters more than a CVSS score
item.description: After PHP2Shell flaws that attackers targeted before a patch shipped, the article argues limiting identity and access matters as much as fixing bugs.

item.title: Kentucky man becomes the first humanist granted religious exemption from AI
Amazon gives Alexa night vision and a bedside role in smart home battle
item.description: Amazon unveiled five new Alexa devices on Oct 28, including the 16-inch Echo Show 16 (from US$499.99) and a bedside Echo Time clock.

item.title: Chinese PCB maker Dongshan rises on its Hong Kong debut, after raising ~$1.3B in an IPO, below its $3B goal, at a $30B valuation, amid a tricky IPO market
item.description: Suzhou Dongshan Precision Manufacturing's shares rose on their Hong Kong debut after its IPO raised about $1.3 billion, below its $3 billion goal.

item.title: Chrome and Firefox Updates Patch Over 200 Vulnerabilities
item.description: Chrome 156 fixes 52 security bugs and Firefox 159 fixes 167 security defects, together resolving more than 200 vulnerabilities.

item.title: Free Fire returns to India as Garena launches localized version four years after ban
item.description: Garena launched Free Fire India, a localized standalone version, on October 28, over four years after New Delhi banned the game over security concerns.

item.title: Unitree reports 70% surge in quarterly revenue, though AI investment weighs on net profit
item.description: Unitree reports a 70 per cent revenue jump in the third quarter, but surging research and development costs weigh on core profits The results for the three months ending September 30 showed a continued surge in research and development spending… Why it matters: Shows robotics firms spending heavily on AI software even as core profits come under pressure.

item.title: World Bank sees commodity prices up 23% in 2026 due to Middle East war, other shocks
item.description: World Bank expects commodity prices to rise 23% in 2026, citing the Middle East war, shipping disruptions and high demand for safe-haven assets.

item.title: Elon Musk, Jensen Huang have opposing outlooks on AI neoclouds. Who is likely correct?
item.description: SpaceX's Elon Musk warns of collapses among the more than 200 GPU rental 'neoclouds', while Nvidia's Jensen Huang says robust demand will solve their liquidity crunch.

item.title: Wall Street backbone DTCC brings $30 trillion securities closer to blockchain with major banks
item.description: DTCC's tokenization service went live on Canton Network and Besu, initially covering select large-cap stocks, ETFs and U.S. Treasuries, with 20 firms signed up.

item.title: CVE-2026-20362 | Cisco Finesse Server-Side Request Forgery Vulnerability
item.description: High-severity SSRF flaw CVE-2026-20362 in Cisco Finesse can let unauthenticated remote attackers obtain limited sensitive information from associated services.

item.title: TLS Flaws Found in GoAhead Web Server Used in Hundreds of Millions of Devices
item.description: FoxIO disclosed three TLS flaws in the GoAhead web server, which could keep revoked client certificates working or expose some encrypted sessions to eavesdroppers.

item.title: Uncertainties in approvals and laws can significantly delay subsea cables for ASEAN Power Grid
item.description: A US energy adviser says complex approvals and regulatory uncertainty can delay ASEAN Power Grid undersea cables and urges standardised rules.

item.title: John Ternus posts teaser video ahead of MacBook Pro redesign unveiling
item.description: Apple CEO John Ternus posted a teaser video ahead of an expected Apple unveiling of redesigned MacBook Pro models with touchscreen OLED displays.

item.title: 7 days until TechCrunch Founder Summit: Save up to $100 on your pass before doors open
item.description: TechCrunch Founder Summit takes place November 4 at Boston's SoWa Power Station, with tickets discounted by up to $100 before doors open.

item.title: TikTok is going after Yelp and Google Maps with an in-app restaurant guide
item.description: TikTok launched 'Must Eat', an in-app restaurant guide built on 40 million food-related posts and reviews, that lets users filter, review and book seats.

item.title: Wendy's shares jump 15% as Nelson Peltz's Trian offers $1.4 billion to buy burger chain
item.description: A Nelson Peltz-led group offered $1.4 billion ($7.35 per share in cash) to take Wendy's private, a 20% premium; shares rose about 15%.

item.title: AI boom creates jobs but threatens others, dividing Nevada unions
Hackers now scanning systems for recently-patched Oracle flaw
item.description: Attackers are probing for unpatched systems with CVE-2026-101767, a critical Oracle E-Business Suite flaw Oracle patched on October 20.

item.title: Meta quietly launched Waddle World, a Tamagotchi-like, AI pet-rearing game, in the Philippines in September, calling it a "daily journal disguised as a pet"
item.description: Meta launched Waddle World, a 16-bit Tamagotchi-like AI pet game that can chat and create illustrated journal entries, available only in the Philippines since September.

item.title: On the day of the touchscreen Mac launch, Dynamic Island elements found in macOS 27
item.description: A leaker found Dynamic Island assets in macOS 27 that appear to confirm the expected MacBook Pro display design replacing the notch.

item.title: Exclusive: Numeracle Raises $28M To Keep Legitimate Business Calls From Spam Label
item.description: Numeracle, a McLean, Virginia-based company that verifies businesses and links them to their phone numbers, raised $28 million from Edison Partners.

item.title: All the Amazon Echo devices announced today: Echo Time, Alexa Photo Frame and more
item.description: Amazon unveiled the $500 Echo Show 16, the $200 Echo Time smart alarm clock and the Alexa Photo Frame, plus upgraded Echo speakers.

item.title: Critical 16-Year-Old UEFI Flaw Can Run Code Before Secure Boot on Network-Booting Servers
item.description: A critical 16-year-old UEFI firmware flaw can let attackers run code before the OS loads, but only when a machine boots over the network.

item.title: Bitcoin rebounds above $81,000 as Asian chip rally spills into crypto, pepe jumps 9%
item.description: Bitcoin rose above $81,400 as Asian chip stocks rallied; memecoin pepe gained 9% after Arkham linked wallets holding $51 million of it to Justin Sun.

item.title: Wazuh and AI for Enhanced SOC Workflows
item.description: Describes how AI can augment security operations center analysts, who receive high alert volumes from many sources and spend time correlating them.

item.title: Wilmar’s quarterly profit drops, expects tough operating environment to persist
item.description: Wilmar's third-quarter core net profit fell 25.2% to US$267.3 million, and it expects operating challenges to persist.

item.title: Why the smartest AI models still need human context
item.description: Executives need to double down on human context, since even the best AI model won't deliver desired outcomes without the right context about what is happening.

item.title: Analysis: As Iran war drags on, airlines pull back on fuel hedges and warn on fares
item.description: Airlines are reluctant to lock in new fuel hedges as jet fuel prices are roughly double pre-conflict levels, warning of higher fares instead.

item.title: MAS urges banks to limit exposure or cut ties with clients over clear environmental breaches linked to haze
item.description: MAS told banks to take stronger measures, including limiting exposure or exiting ties, against clients who clearly breach environmental laws, amid scrutiny over haze-linked firms.

item.title: Mapletree Logistics Trust Q2 DPU flat at S$0.01816
item.description: Mapletree Logistics Trust's Q2 distribution per unit was flat at S$0.01816; it plans a S$141 million Changi South warehouse redevelopment, due 2Q 2029.

item.title: WebAI by Opera
item.description: Opera's WebAI lets websites use AI models running on your own computer.

item.title: Access Video and Image Models from Figma Weave via the Figma MCP
item.description: Figma Weave's image and video models can now be used inside external AI agents via the Figma MCP, consuming Weave credits.

item.title: Hacker Drains Nearly $1M in SOL From Solana Trading Bot Users in 94 Seconds
item.description: Bloom says attackers drained about $947,000 in SOL from 49 wallets of nine users of its Telegram trading bot, exploiting a third-party module.

item.title: Tears of the Kingdom, running native on iPhone Duo!
item.description: A port runs Tears of the Kingdom natively on the iPhone Duo with controller support, DualSense haptics and folded or unfolded play.

item.title: EmbeddingGemma 2: Unified and Efficient Multimodal Representations
item.description: EmbeddingGemma 2 is an open model that represents text, images, audio and video in one space, beating specialist and larger models on benchmarks.

item.title: Amazon Lists 250 Million Products From Rival Sites in Effort to Battle Agents
item.description: Amazon now has 250 million listings linking to products sold elsewhere, about 2.5 times as many as in March, via its Shop Direct initiative. This could give shoppers less reason to use outside AI shopping tools. Why it matters: Shows Amazon blocking outside shopping agents and steering shoppers to its own listings as new AI assistants raise the stakes.
